title: Darfur conflict (ongoing genocide and humanitarian crisis)
description: Armed conflict between government-aligned Janjaweed militias and rebel groups continued across Darfur throughout 2006, marked by attacks on civilians, mass displacement and a severe humanitarian crisis. A September 2006 study published in the journal Science estimated at least 200,000 deaths since the conflict began in 2003, with estimates up to 300,000-400,000 cited by the UN Secretary-General and other organizations, most deaths resulting from violence, disease and starvation. The Darfur Peace Agreement signed in May 2006 failed to end the fighting, and more than two million people remained displaced.

review.note: Science publication date is September 15, 2006, not an event onset. Its mortality estimate is cumulative since 2003 and would overlap earlier Darfur records; January 1,2006 is unsupported as a specific event date. Primary study and GAO discuss uncertainty; do not treat 200,000 as additional deaths during 2006.

sources.name: Hagan and Palloni, Death in Darfur

title: Iraq War (2007)
description: Iraq Body Count's current database records 26,112 civilian deaths from violence during calendar year 2007. This full-year total includes separately recorded attacks and is not a death count for January 1.

review.note: 26,112 matches current IBC annual database, not January1 deaths. January1 is an annual-index placeholder and cannot be verified as a discrete event date. Remove unsupported causal assertion linking annual deaths to surge and military-death comparison; annual total overlaps individual attacks.

sources.name: Iraq Body Count current annual database

title: Kenya post-election violence
description: Violence followed Kenya's disputed December 2007 election and continued into February 2008. The Waki commission recorded 1,133 deaths during its December 27, 2007-February 29, 2008 assessment period. The toll includes killings across multiple provinces, not one January 1 incident.

review.note: Waki commission supports1,133 deaths in the December27-February29 inquiry period. January1 is not the onset; reported first violence, declaration and inquiry dates differ. Correct toll/geographic scope, but do not replace uncertain onset with another unqualified date. Mediation was African Union-led, not simply UN-brokered.

title: China winter storms (2008 Chinese snowstorms)
description: A series of snow, freezing-rain and severe-cold episodes affected southern and central China beginning January 10, 2008, disrupting electricity and transport. The Asian Disaster Reduction Center's subsequent summary records 129 deaths across 20 provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities.

title: Mustansiriya University bombing
description: Bombing attacks near Mustansiriya University in Baghdad on January 16, 2007, killed about 70 people, many of them students, according to UNAMI. Numerous others were injured.

title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
description: Israel's military offensive against Hamas in the Gaza Strip ran from December 27, 2008, to a ceasefire on January 18, 2009. Human rights organizations and UN agencies documented approximately 1,340-1,400 Palestinians killed, including around 750-770 civilians and more than 300 children, with over 5,000 wounded. Thirteen Israelis were killed, including 3 civilians. The offensive included heavy air strikes and ground operations and caused extensive destruction of homes, schools, and infrastructure across Gaza.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
Al Mezan Centre for Human Rights

review.note: Campaign dates corroborated. B'Tselem snapshots give 1,387 and 1,385 Palestinian deaths, not a final exact 1,400. The numeric field does not specify whether the 13 Israeli deaths are included. Civilian definitions differ; 5,000 wounded and infrastructure claims need their own evidence.

title: al-Sadriya market bombing
description: A suicide truck bomb struck Baghdad's Sadriya market on February 3, 2007. Contemporary reports and an FBI retrospective give at least 135 deaths, while Iraq Body Count's current incident record gives 136-137.

review.note: Wrong market: Sadriya, not Shorja. FBI retrospective records135; current IBC136-137. Date and afternoon timing secure, but exact mortality not reconciled. Correct identity without treating conflicting final counts as settled.

title: Sunjiawan coal mine explosion
description: A gas explosion at the Sunjiawan coal mine's Haizhou shaft in Fuxin, Liaoning, on February 14, 2005, killed 214 people and injured 30, according to the official investigation.
sources: China Ministry of Emergency Management investigation

title: Southern Leyte mudslide buries Guinsaugon village
description: A major landslide buried Guinsaugon village in Saint Bernard, Southern Leyte, on February 17, 2006, after prolonged heavy rain. Homes and an elementary school were buried. IFRC's subsequent report records 1,126 deaths.
sources: Center for Excellence in Disaster Management

title: Kandahar dog-fighting show suicide bombing
description: A suicide bombing struck a crowd watching a dog-fighting competition near Kandahar on February 17, 2008. A local police commander was among those killed. UNAMA recorded 67 civilian deaths, while provincial reporting gave a higher overall toll.

review.note: UNAMA annual report records67 civilian deaths; governor's contemporary account reports over100 overall. Armed police/guards may explain some difference but no reconciled breakdown was obtained.100 is not an exact count when source says over100. Date and gathering supported; attribution/ranking can be omitted but mortality remains core blocker.

title: Samjhauta Express bombing
description: Bombs and fire struck two coaches of the Samjhauta Express near Panipat shortly before midnight on February 18, 2007. Later court reporting records 68 people killed, most of them Pakistani nationals.

title: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion
description: A disaster at the Pasta de Conchos coal mine in Coahuila on February 19, 2006, killed 65 miners. Only two bodies were recovered during the earlier recovery efforts, leaving families campaigning for the recovery of the remaining victims. Renewed recovery operations later located additional remains.

title: Zarand earthquake
description: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck near Zarand in Kerman Province, Iran, levelling several mud-brick mountain villages and killing 612 people. An estimated 80,000 people were affected and more than 900 were injured.

review.note: USGS supports Mw 6.4 and February 22. Summary attributes 612 deaths to PAGER-CAT but also reports an independent ISNA count of 799. Need source-level resolution of mortality scope and the 80,000 affected/900 injured figures before full verification.

title: Al-Askari shrine bombing triggers sectarian violence
description: Bombers dressed as security personnel detonated explosives inside the al-Askari shrine in Samarra on February 22, 2006, destroying the golden dome of one of Shia Islam's holiest sites. The blast itself killed no one, but it triggered waves of retaliatory sectarian killings across Iraq, with more than 1,000 people dead within days and hundreds of mosques attacked; leaked U.S. military documents later indicated the death toll exceeded 3,000, and the bombing is widely regarded as having ignited Iraq's civil war.

review.note: Shrine blast itself killed nobody. Subsequent1000/1300/3000 estimates refer to different periods/areas and cannot become a single Samarra bombing toll; they also overlap annual Iraq record. Need a bounded reprisal-event definition. Do not fabricate a positive bombing death count to satisfy schema.

title: Iraq sectarian civil war (deadliest year of the conflict)
description: Sectarian violence intensified in Iraq in 2006. Iraq Body Count's current database records 29,526 civilian deaths from violence during the full calendar year. This annual total includes numerous separately recorded attacks and is not the toll of the February 22 shrine bombing.
sources: United Nations Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI)

review.note: IBC current annual table gives29,526 for all2006; February22 indexes a catalyst, not the start of that count. January-February deaths and other discrete events overlap. UNAMI uses a different methodology, not simply matching IBC. Annual/single-event schema and double counting must be resolved.

title: Hilla suicide car bombing
description: A suicide car bombing struck people waiting outside a clinic in Hilla on February 28, 2005, including applicants for government security jobs. Early reports counted at least 125 dead; Iraq Body Count's current incident table records 135-136.

review.note: 125 was early reporting. IBC's current table gives 135-136 although its heading still says 125-136; another summary gives 127. Date and clinic bombing are secure, final fatality total is not. Remove superlative and broad victim characterization.

title: Karrada double bombing in Baghdad
description: Two explosions struck Baghdad's Karrada shopping district on March 6, 2008. The second occurred as people gathered to help victims of the first. Subsequent reporting put the death toll at 68.

title: Winnenden School Shooting
description: On March 11, 2009, 17-year-old former student Tim Kretschmer killed 15 people in a shooting spree beginning at his former school in Winnenden, Germany, and ending in nearby Wendlingen. He later died by suicide, bringing the total number of deaths to 16 including the attacker.

title: Ulyanovskaya mine disaster
description: A methane explosion at the Ulyanovskaya coal mine near Novokuznetsk on March 19, 2007, killed 110 of the 203 people underground. Ninety-three survived, according to IFRC.

title: Red Lake High School shooting
description: On March 21, 2005, a 16-year-old killed his grandfather and his grandfather's companion before attacking Red Lake High School. He killed a security guard, a teacher and five students there, then died by suicide. Ten people died in total, including the attacker.

title: Battle of Mogadishu (2007)
description: Ethiopian and Somali government forces fought insurgents in Mogadishu during major offensives in March and April 2007. Human Rights Watch documented extensive civilian harm but said precise mortality figures could not be established.

review.note: HRW dates main first offensive March29-April2, second round endingApril26, and explicitly cannot give precise civilian deaths. Estimates400-1,000 first round plus about300 second are not an independently established1,200. March21 onset and annual6,000/superlative remain unverified.

title: Capitol Hill massacre in Seattle
description: Kyle Huff killed six people and wounded two at a house party in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighborhood on March 25, 2006. He then died by suicide when confronted by police, bringing the total number of deaths to seven, including the attacker.

title: Tal Afar truck bombings
description: Truck bombs struck markets in Tal Afar on March 27, 2007, collapsing buildings. Iraq Body Count records 152 deaths; a US Army history reports nearly 350 wounded. Subsequent reprisal killings are not included in this bombing toll.
sources: US Army Iraq War history volume2

title: Nias-Simeulue earthquake
description: A magnitude 8.6 earthquake struck off northern Sumatra on March 28, 2005, severely damaging Nias and nearby islands and generating a relatively small tsunami. Published death estimates vary; most fatalities occurred on Nias.

review.note: Magnitude 8.6 and March 28 UTC are secure. Later summaries span 915-1,314 while early relief estimates were higher; hundreds on Simeulue/Banyak are not established as final confirmed counts. Need final regional breakdown rather than combining initial estimates.

title: Borujerd (Silakhor) earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck the Silakhor plain region of Lorestan province in western Iran on March 31, 2006, early in the morning, centered near the village of Darb-e Astaneh. The quake killed about 70 people, injured more than 1,200 and damaged or destroyed buildings in roughly 330 villages, with the worst destruction in Borujerd and Dorud.
sources: International Institute of Earthquake Engineering and Seismology (IIEES)

review.note: Early IFRC and JICA reports give70; IFRC's April2007 retrospective instead gives63 deaths and1,418 injured. Mainshock March31 01:17UTC and Mw6.1 established, but revised mortality discrepancy is not reconciled.

title: Solomon Islands earthquake and tsunami
location: Western and Choiseul provinces, Solomon Islands
description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake struck near Gizo at 20:39 UTC on April 1, 2007, the morning of April 2 locally, generating a destructive tsunami. The earthquake and tsunami killed 52 people in the Solomon Islands. The national disaster office's subsequent reconciliation reported no people still missing.

title: Binghamton Immigration Center Shooting
description: On April 3, 2009, a gunman attacked the American Civic Association in Binghamton, New York, killing 13 people and wounding four. The attacker then died by suicide, bringing the total deaths including him to 14.

title: L'Aquila Earthquake
description: An earthquake struck Abruzzo and the city of L'Aquila at 3:32 a.m. local time on April 6, 2009. Italian Civil Protection records 309 deaths and more than 1,500 injuries. About 65,000 people were displaced.

title: Virginia Tech shooting
description: On April 16, 2007, a student gunman killed 32 people and wounded 17 by gunfire in two attacks at Virginia Tech in Blacksburg, Virginia. Other people suffered injuries while escaping. The attacker died by suicide and is excluded from the 32 victims.
sources: Virginia Tech Review Panel via US DOJ

title: al-Sadriya market bombing
description: A car bomb exploded at Baghdad's Sadriya food market on the afternoon of April 18, 2007. Iraq Body Count records 140 deaths in this attack, excluding other bombings across Baghdad that day.

title: Amagasaki train derailment
description: A JR West commuter train derailed and struck an apartment building in Amagasaki on April 25, 2005. It entered a 70 km/h curve at about 116 km/h. The crash killed 107 people, including the driver, and injured 562.

title: Cyclone Nargis strikes Myanmar
description: Cyclone Nargis struck Myanmar on May 2-3, 2008, devastating the Ayeyarwady Delta and other areas. The joint government, ASEAN and UN assessment reported 84,537 deaths and 53,836 people missing as of June 24. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing. About 2.4 million people were severely affected.

title: Wenchuan earthquake (Sichuan earthquake)
description: The Wenchuan earthquake struck Sichuan on May 12, 2008, at 14:28 local time, damaging towns and infrastructure across the region. Later official figures cited in engineering research were 69,227 deaths, 17,923 missing and 374,643 injured. The recorded toll includes reported deaths only, excluding the missing.
sources: Earthquake Engineering Field Investigation Team study

title: Jaipur bombings
description: A series of bombs exploded in Jaipur's old city on the evening of May 13, 2008. Later court reporting records 71 deaths and 185 injuries. Four men convicted in the serial-blast case were acquitted by the High Court in 2023; four men were convicted in a separate related unexploded-bomb case in 2025.

title: Sri Lankan Civil War Final Offensive
description: Between January and May 2009, the Sri Lankan military's final offensive against the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) trapped roughly 330,000 civilians in an ever-shrinking 'no fire zone' in the northeast. A UN Secretary-General-appointed panel of experts estimated in 2011 that as many as 40,000 civilians were killed, most by government shelling, with the LTTE also accused of using civilians as human shields. The government's own figures put the toll at about 7,000-9,000. The war ended on May 18, 2009, with the military declaring victory.

review.note: 40,000 is an upper estimate cited by the UN panel, not a confirmed count. AP corroborates tens of thousands and abuses by both sides. Government 7,000-9,000 attribution and the precise 330,000 trapped figure remain unestablished. The military defeat on May 18 and presidential victory declaration on May 19 must not be conflated.

title: Cyclone Aila
description: Cyclone Aila, a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, made landfall on May 25, 2009, near the Bangladesh-India border, bringing storm surges of up to 6 meters. Final official tallies recorded about 339 deaths across the region, including roughly 190 in Bangladesh and 140 in eastern India's West Bengal state, with hundreds of thousands left homeless and millions affected by flooding and breached embankments.
sources: University of Colorado Natural Hazards Center

review.note: Aila and May 25 landfall corroborated, but 339 as a final official regional count and the 190/140 split were not established. IMD-hosted assessment describes a 3 m surge in western Bangladesh; the claimed 6 m maximum needs a location-specific source. Satkhira is narrower than the regional toll.

title: Yogyakarta earthquake
description: An earthquake struck the Yogyakarta and Central Java regions at about 05:54 on May 27, 2006, local time, May 26 UTC. Bantul and Klaten suffered severe damage. A subsequent IFRC report cites an official toll of 5,749 deaths and more than 38,000 injuries.

title: Typhoon Fengshen (Frank) and MV Princess of the Stars sinking
description: Typhoon Fengshen crossed the Philippines beginning on June 20, 2008, causing destructive flooding. During the storm, the ferry MV Princess of the Stars capsized near Sibuyan Island on June 21. Philippine disaster-agency reporting in July counted 557 deaths apart from the ferry disaster; a reconciled final combined toll is not established here.

review.note: The June 20 Philippine landfall is supported by HKO; June 25 was the later China landfall. NDCC reporting gives 557 deaths excluding the ferry (GMA, July 10), whereas ADRC's July 31 snapshot also lists 87 missing. The original 1,371, the ferry's asserted 800-850 deaths, and the Philippines/China aggregation were not reconciled with a final official passenger and casualty accounting. Do not add bodies recovered, presumed deaths and missing passengers indiscriminately. The shortened description removes the unsupported attribution of 1,371 to government/UN and the superlative; the numeric toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Hong Kong Observatory: tropical cyclones in 2008
GMA News: NDCC damage and casualty report, July 10, 2008
Asian Disaster Reduction Center: Philippines typhoon record

title: Cyclone Yemyin and Pakistan floods
description: Cyclone Yemyin made landfall on Pakistan's Makran coast on June 26, 2007, bringing torrential rain and flash floods that killed about 730 people in Balochistan, Sindh, and the North-West Frontier Province, with more than 100 killed in Afghanistan. Preceding heavy rain had already caused flooding and hundreds of deaths in Karachi.

review.note: 730 is a Pakistan-wide multistorm/flood figure in secondary summaries, not established as deaths from June26 Yemyin alone. IFRC documents storms fromJune23 and later flooding; final-report body retrieval failed. Need exact geographic/date scope and independently supported mortality before publication.

title: Niger food crisis
description: Severe drought and a locust infestation triggered a food crisis in Niger affecting 3.6 million people, with UNICEF reporting 32,000 severely malnourished children under five facing death without treatment. A final death toll was never established; UN officials said thousands of children had already died, with overall mortality estimates ranging from several thousand to tens of thousands.

review.note: No checked source establishes 10,000 crisis-attributable deaths or a July 1 onset. UNICEF and the national mortality survey describe malnutrition, treatment and rates; children at risk are not observed fatalities. Do not infer a toll by multiplying treatment mortality or projected deaths. Numeric entry requires exclusion from aggregates pending evidence.

title: London bombings (7/7)
description: Four suicide bombers attacked three London Underground trains and a bus on July 7, 2005. The attacks killed 52 people, excluding the bombers, and injured more than 770.

title: Indian embassy bombing in Kabul
description: A suicide vehicle bombing struck the Indian embassy in Kabul on the morning of July 7, 2008. India's foreign ministry identified four Indian officials and one Afghan embassy employee among those killed. UNAMA subsequently recorded 55 civilian deaths; reported overall totals differ.

review.note: July 7 morning and the embassy identity are supported by MEA. Four Indian officials and one Afghan employee were killed, so four Indian staff is not the entire embassy-staff toll. MEA's 2008-09 annual report says about 60 Afghan nationals plus five embassy personnel; UNAMA's annual report counts 55 civilians, while secondary accounts give 58 overall. These differing populations and totals cannot be assumed equivalent. A previously indexed 2010 MEA PDF returned a 404 on opening and is not treated as primary verification of 58. Removed unsupported police/child subtotals, queue composition and superlative; overall toll remains unresolved.

sources.name: Ministry of External Affairs: annual report 2008-2009
Ministry of External Affairs: foreign relations 2008, July 7 statement
UNAMA: protection of civilians annual report 2008
Wikipedia: 2008 Indian embassy bombing, secondary comparison

title: Mumbai train bombings
description: Seven explosions struck suburban trains on Mumbai's Western Line during the evening rush hour on July 11, 2006. Later court reporting gives 189 deaths, differing from the 209 figure in some earlier accounts. Responsibility and the prosecution evidence have been disputed in court.

review.note: Modern court coverage gives189 deaths/824 injured rather than209. The High Court rejected the prosecution case in July2025; subsequent Supreme Court stay did not itself establish guilt. Remove asserted pressure-cooker mechanism and categorical attribution; final victim count requires reconciliation.

title: 2006 Lebanon War
description: The war between Israel and Hezbollah lasted from July 12 to August 14, 2006. Human Rights Watch reported at least 1,109 deaths in Lebanon, mostly civilians, and about one million displaced people. The recorded toll is for Lebanon only; Israeli deaths are not included.

title: Tropical Storm Bilis floods and landslides in China
description: Severe Tropical Storm Bilis made landfall on mainland China on July 14, 2006. Its prolonged rainfall caused extensive flooding and landslides across southern China. A meteorological study citing the China Meteorological Administration reports at least 843 deaths.

title: North Korea floods and food crisis
description: Floods struck several North Korean provinces in July 2006, damaging homes, farmland and infrastructure. Published death and missing-person counts differed widely, and independent assessment was limited.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)

review.note: 600 conflates uncertain killed/missing reporting. Sources range from Red Cross151 dead to a pro-North Korean newspaper's549 dead/295 missing; outside claims are unverified. WFP describes assistance stocks used for2006 floods, so blanket rejection of relief is misleading. Exact episode onset and toll remain unresolved.

title: Pangandaran earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake off Java on July 17, 2006, generated a tsunami that struck about 300 kilometres of southern coastline, including Pangandaran. A field-survey study reports 668 deaths, 65 people missing and 9,299 receiving medical treatment.

title: Sharm el-Sheikh bombings
description: Bombs struck Sharm el-Sheikh shortly after 01:00 on July 23, 2005, local time, July 22 UTC. Targets included the Old Market and a hotel. Death reports differed: the official count was 64, while hospitals reported 88.

review.note: 01:15 Egyptian summer time July 23 equals 22:15 UTC July 22. IFRC's later report uses 64 deaths and 124 injured, while hospital-based accounts reported 88 and 200. Correct UTC date but retain fatality conflict explicitly.

title: Mumbai floods
description: Exceptional rain on July 26-27, 2005, caused severe flooding in Mumbai and other parts of Maharashtra. The Santacruz observatory measured 944 mm over 24 hours. Reported mortality totals differ in geographic and flood-related disease coverage.

review.note: 944 mm is the Santacruz station's 24-hour measurement, not citywide rainfall. 1,094 is commonly a Maharashtra-wide count, while some papers incorrectly or differently label it Mumbai-only; NIDM distinguishes municipal deaths. Establish regional/flood-versus-disease scope before accepting exact toll.

title: Ahmedabad serial bombings
description: A series of bombings in Ahmedabad on July 26, 2008 killed 56 people and injured more than 200. The targets included hospitals. In February 2022, a special court sentenced 38 defendants to death and 11 to life imprisonment in the bombing case.
sources: The Indian Express: Ahmedabad bombing sentences, February 18, 2022
Ministry of Home Affairs: tribunal order published August 6, 2024

title: Ethiopia floods (Dire Dawa and Omo Valley)
description: Unusually intense seasonal rains in August 2006 caused two major flood disasters in Ethiopia: a flash flood of the Dechatu River in the city of Dire Dawa on August 6 killed 256 people with about 250 missing, and flooding of the Omo River in the remote South Omo Valley on August 13 killed 364 people and submerged five villages. Combined flood deaths across the country in 2006 reached about 640, with roughly 118,000 people affected and tens of thousands displaced.
sources: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)

review.note: IFRC's August response reported639, not640; AfDB's full2006 account includes later floods and about900 deaths. Do not merge August and annual scopes. August6 is the local Dire Dawa date, not established onset of all nationwide flooding or confirmed UTC date.

title: Russo-Georgian War
description: Heavy fighting began around Tskhinvali in South Ossetia on the night of August 7-8, 2008 and expanded into a five-day war involving Georgian and Russian forces and separatist forces. The EU fact-finding mission estimated about 850 deaths across the conflict from the parties' reported losses and said far more than 100,000 civilians fled their homes.
sources: EU Independent International Fact-Finding Mission: volume I
Human Rights Watch: Up in Flames, January 2009
Human Rights Watch: cluster-munition investigation, April 2009

title: Typhoon Morakot
description: Typhoon Morakot, the deadliest typhoon to hit Taiwan in about 50 years, made landfall on August 7-8, 2009, dumping record rainfall of up to 3 meters in the southern mountains. A massive mudslide buried the village of Xiaolin in Kaohsiung County, killing an estimated 400-500 residents. More than 670 people were confirmed dead in Taiwan, with additional deaths in China and the northern Philippines, for a regional total of roughly 700-800 lives lost.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: Taiwan reconstruction record lists 681 dead and 18 missing separately; paper dates the typhoon strike to August 7. Existing 700 is an untraceable rounded regional total. Need landfall time/UTC, final cross-country sum and Xiaolin toll before replacing date or numeric field.

title: Typhoon Saomai strikes China
description: Typhoon Saomai made landfall in Zhejiang on August 10, 2006. The Hong Kong Observatory's annual account records at least 460 deaths across Zhejiang, Fujian and Jiangxi, about two million people evacuated and 60,000 houses destroyed.

title: Qahtaniya Yazidi community bombings
description: Coordinated suicide vehicle bombings struck Yazidi communities near Sinjar, including Qahtaniya and Jazira, on August 14, 2007. Hundreds of people died. Published mortality figures differ substantially, and the exact total remains unresolved in this audit.

review.note: IBC currently records516-525, versus796 in secondary summaries attributed to Red Crescent and lower government/early counts. Primary Red Crescent documentation establishing796 was not located. Event date/towns and coordinated attacks supported; final count and1,500 injuries unresolved.

title: Peru earthquake
description: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake struck off central Peru on August 15, 2007, severely damaging Pisco and nearby communities and producing a tsunami. A USGS-funded research report cites an October 2007 Peruvian statistical count of 595 deaths, with missing people listed separately.

review.note: USGS-supported research report cites595 deaths plus318 missing as an October2 INEI figure; these are separate categories. Other summaries repeat519, so attribute595 explicitly rather than universal final count. Replace85percent destroyed with supported general damage; date23:40UTC unchanged. The differing 519/595 accounts have not been reconciled by reporting period and finalization; the attributed candidate prose does not by itself establish final mortality. Withhold pending that reconciliation.

title: Abidjan toxic waste dumping (Probo Koala)
description: Waste discharged from the Probo Koala was dumped by a local contractor at multiple sites around Abidjan on August 19, 2006. UNEP records more than 100,000 medical consultations afterward. Reported death counts and the extent of medically established causal links differ between sources.

review.note: UNEP describes528 cubic metres and12 sites, Amnesty at least18 sites and an official15-death report, while17 appears in later government-attributed summaries. More than100,000 consultations are not proof of100,000 poisoning hospitalizations. Exact mortality and causal attribution remain unsettled; preserve distinctions.

title: Les Issers police academy suicide bombing
description: A vehicle bombing outside the gendarmerie training school at Les Issers on August 19, 2008 struck people waiting for an entrance examination. Algeria's Interior Ministry reported 43 victims killed, comprising 42 civilians and one police officer, and 45 people injured.
sources: Amnesty International: Les Issers and Bouira bombings
AFP via La Depeche: Les Issers bombing, August 19, 2008
EFE via Listin Diario: preliminary report of 44 deaths

title: Baghdad Ministry Bombings
description: On August 19, 2009, coordinated truck bombings hit the Iraqi Foreign Ministry and Finance Ministry in Baghdad, along with other explosions, killing at least 95 people and wounding about 563 according to Iraqi Interior Ministry officials. The attacks, blamed on al-Qaeda-linked militants and Baathist elements, were the bloodiest day in Baghdad since February 2008 and the worst since US troops withdrew from Iraqi cities at the end of June 2009.

review.note: Reuters photograph corroborates ministry attack and August 19 date. The searches did not independently establish 95/563, the comparative superlatives or final perpetrator attribution; BBC access was blocked. Keep unverified until a casualty report is checked. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

title: Azizabad airstrike
description: A US-led operation struck Azizabad in Herat Province at approximately 02:00 local time on August 22, 2008 (August 21 UTC). UNAMA's annual report subsequently counted 92 civilian deaths, including 62 children. The civilian death toll remained disputed between investigations.

review.note: AIHRC places the attack at approximately 02:00 Afghanistan time on August 22, corresponding to August 21 UTC; propose the UTC correction without changing the original identity key. UNAMA's later annual report gives 92 civilian deaths including 62 children, not the initial 90/60, while the US investigation reported 33. The competing investigations have not been reconciled and 90 cannot be certified as a final total. Remove unverified compensation and aircraft detail, retain the contradiction in notes, and withhold the row pending a settled toll policy/evidence.

sources.name: Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission: report submitted to UN Human Rights Council
UNAMA: protection of civilians annual report 2008
Wikipedia: Azizabad airstrike, competing investigation totals

title: Greek forest fires
description: Widespread forest fires in Greece, most severely in the Peloponnese, burned from late August 2007 and killed 85 people across the country. Flames raced through villages, and many victims were trapped in their homes or while fleeing by car.

review.note: 85 is a summer/season total in secondary accounts, not established for fires beginningAugust24. European Commission study gives76 for2007, while secondary accounts distinguish67 inAugust. Need authoritative mortality reconciliation and defined episode start; July fires cannot be silently moved toAugust24.

title: Hurricane Katrina
location: US Gulf Coast, including Louisiana and Mississippi
description: Hurricane Katrina struck the northern US Gulf Coast on August 29, 2005, causing catastrophic storm surge and flooding. New Orleans suffered extensive inundation after flood-protection failures. The National Weather Service's updated assessment attributes 1,392 deaths and $125 billion in damage, in 2005 dollars, to the hurricane.

title: Al-Aaimmah bridge stampede
description: A stampede on the Al-Aaimmah bridge in Baghdad during a Shia pilgrimage killed at least 965 people, mostly women and children crushed or drowned in the Tigris River after rumours of a suicide bomber sparked panic. The stampede followed mortar fire near the Kadhimiya shrine that had already killed pilgrims.

review.note: 965 appears in retrospective summaries, while contemporary RTE gives 956 and forecasts 1,000. Need final official count and confirmation that earlier mortar victims are excluded. This was a crowd crush triggered by a reported bomber rumor, not an established suicide bombing; terrorism categorization needs taxonomy review.

title: Kunduz Fuel Tanker Airstrike
description: On September 4, 2009, NATO aircraft, at the request of German forces, bombed two fuel tankers hijacked by Taliban insurgents near Kunduz City. Villagers had gathered around the stranded tankers to siphon fuel. Death toll estimates range from 56 to 179, with a German parliamentary investigation concluding up to 142 people died, including more than 100 civilians. The strike sparked a major political crisis in Germany and led to compensation payments to victims' families.

review.note: Bundestag says the exact number remains unknown and cites reports up to 142; it does not establish over 100 civilians as the parliamentary conclusion. Numeric 100 is unsupported precision. Also verify local overnight strike against UTC before retaining September 4. Do not replace it with a different estimate as a confirmed count.

title: Malegaon bombings
description: Four explosions struck Malegaon on September 8, 2006, around Friday prayers. The Bombay High Court's later account records 31 deaths and 312 injuries. In April 2026, the court discharged the last four accused, leaving no accused facing trial in this case at that time.

title: Chinese melamine milk scandal
description: In 2008, melamine deliberately added to diluted milk contaminated infant formula and other milk products in China. A WHO-authored review reported six deaths, 294,000 affected children and 51,900 cumulative hospitalizations as of December 1, 2008. The exact beginning of the contamination and resulting illness was unknown; the problem became public in September.

review.note: The WHO-authored review supports six reported deaths, 294,000 cases and 51,900 cumulative hospitalizations as of December 1, not 50,000 people simultaneously hospitalized at the peak. It says the illness/contamination onset is unknown, with complaints in December 2007 and a first death in May 2008. September 17 marks Singapore's first detection outside China, not the start of the Chinese scandal. No replacement exact onset date is established. Remove unsupported withdrawal tonnage and arrest detail; the supported shorter description does not cure the unresolved date.

sources.name: WHO authors in Environmental Health Perspectives: The Melamine Incident
Food Policy: China's milk scandal and its institutional roots

title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
description: A suicide truck bombing struck the Marriott Hotel in Islamabad on the evening of September 20, 2008, causing a major fire and killing dozens. A group calling itself Fedayeen Islam later claimed responsibility, but that claim was not authenticated in the contemporaneous Reuters report.

review.note: September 20 evening is established, but the exact victim total is not: the US State Department's annual report says 53, the original says 54, and a 2012 US court opinion cites 56 from BBC reporting. These are not demonstrated to be solely attacker-inclusion differences. The statement that no group claimed responsibility is false: Reuters reported a Fedayeen Islam claim on September 22 while explicitly saying it was unauthenticated. Remove the unsupported explosive weight, nationality breakdown and ranking; preserve the unverified nature of that claim. Toll remains a publication blocker.

sources.name: US State Department: Pakistan human rights report 2008
Reuters via RFE/RL: unauthenticated responsibility claim
US District Court: DiFederico v Marriott memorandum opinion

title: Typhoon Ketsana (Ondoy)
description: Tropical storm Ketsana (Ondoy) struck the Philippines on September 26, 2009, bringing the heaviest rainfall to Metro Manila in more than four decades — about a month's rain in under 12 hours — and causing catastrophic flash flooding. The consolidated regional death toll reached roughly 900, including 671 in the Philippines, 179 in Vietnam, and dozens more in Cambodia and Laos. Hundreds of thousands were displaced across Southeast Asia.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: JICA cites 464 Philippine deaths; GMA's 277 is explicitly an October 1 preliminary count. Neither supports 671 Philippine deaths or the 921 regional field. Need comparable final country reports; do not add preliminary and final or Ondoy/Pepeng totals.

title: Samoa Earthquake and Tsunami
description: A magnitude 8.1 earthquake near the Samoan Islands on September 29, 2009, generated destructive tsunami waves. NOAA records 192 deaths: 149 in Samoa, 34 in American Samoa and nine in Tonga. Runup exceeded 22 meters in Tonga.

title: West Sumatra (Padang) Earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck off the coast of West Sumatra on September 30, 2009, about 45 km northwest of Padang. The Indonesian government confirmed 1,115 deaths, with more than 1,200 seriously injured and about 450,000 people displaced. Widespread collapse of poorly reinforced buildings in Padang and Padang Pariaman district caused most casualties. USGS called it the deadliest earthquake of 2009.

review.note: Date, Padang/Pariaman area and magnitude corroborated by assessment material; retrieved assessment gives over 1,117, not 1,115. Exact final toll, displacement and strongest mortality ranking need reconciliation with BNPB/USGS, rather than selecting a convenient near-match.

title: Bali bombings
description: Three suicide bombers attacked restaurants in Kuta and Jimbaran, Bali, on October 1, 2005. Twenty victims were killed and more than 100 people injured. Including the three bombers, 23 people died.

title: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng)
description: Typhoon Parma (Pepeng) made landfall in northern Luzon on October 3, 2009, and lingered over the island for a week, making landfall three times and causing torrential rains. Massive landslides in Benguet province and the Cordillera Administrative Region killed 465 people in the Philippines, with total regional deaths near 500, including in Vietnam and China. Landslide-buried villages in La Trinidad and Baguio City accounted for the heaviest losses.
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

review.note: Search located an NDCC-attributed 465 Philippine tally but not a directly inspected final official report. Regional 500, non-Philippine deaths and the claim that landslides alone caused all 465 require corroboration. Secondary lead is not sufficient to verify this record. Only one checked source is recorded; the two-source publication minimum is not met.

title: Hurricane Stan
description: Hurricane Stan triggered torrential rain and catastrophic mudslides across Guatemala, El Salvador and southern Mexico, burying entire villages including Panabaj near Lake Atitlan, where about 1,400 residents were declared missing and presumed dead. More than 1,600 people were killed across the region, most of them in Guatemala.

review.note: NOAA authors distinguish 80 direct Stan deaths from 1,000-2,000 deaths in the broader regional weather system. October 5 is near dissipation, not landfall; the Panabaj estimate and exact 1,660 aggregate are not established. Needs explicit regional episode scope and onset.

title: Kashmir earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Muzaffarabad in Pakistani-administered Kashmir, collapsing tens of thousands of poorly built homes and schools and killing an estimated 75,000 people in Pakistan and more than 1,300 in India, with regional estimates reaching 87,000. About 3.5 million people were left homeless.

review.note: Original 75,000 does not match its own Pakistan-plus-India narrative. OCHA uses over 73,000 in Pakistan; other sources give 87,350 and higher regional totals. Magnitude/date established; final geographic and mortality-estimate basis must be chosen explicitly.

title: Baghdad Justice Ministry Bombings
description: On October 25, 2009, two suicide car bombs exploded in quick succession near the Iraqi Ministry of Justice and the Baghdad Provincial Council building, killing at least 155 people and wounding more than 500. Victims included about two dozen children riding a bus near the Justice Ministry daycare. The Islamic State of Iraq, an al-Qaeda-linked group, claimed responsibility. It was Iraq's deadliest attack in more than two years.

title: Balochistan earthquake
description: A magnitude-6.4 earthquake struck Balochistan on October 28, 2008 UTC, in the early morning of October 29 locally, severely damaging villages in the Ziarat area. IFRC reporting recorded 166 deaths and hundreds of injuries; other published death totals differ.

review.note: The first destructive magnitude-6.4 shock was October 28 at 23:09 UTC, October 29 locally; another large shock occurred October 29 UTC. Propose October 28 for the first shock. IFRC's initial appeal update and later Pakistan plan report 166 deaths, whereas the original calls 215 final and inconsistently says official reports had reached 236. Those alternative totals are not reconciled. IFRC's roughly 122,000 refers to people affected, not all homeless. Remove that conflation and the unsupported failed-appeal story. The ASC event page was indexed but could not be opened; the exact UTC time is also given in the secondary earthquake record.

sources.name: IFRC: Pakistan earthquake appeal update MDRPK00201
Amateur Seismic Centre: October 28, 2008 Balochistan earthquake
Wikipedia: 2008 Ziarat earthquakes, UTC event times

title: Peshawar Meena Bazaar Bombing
description: On October 28, 2009, a car bomb exploded in the Meena Bazaar, a women's market in Peshawar, killing approximately 110-120 people — about 70 of them women and children — and injuring more than 200. The blast, among the deadliest attacks in Peshawar's history, destroyed several buildings and trapped many victims in rubble. Pakistani Taliban-linked militants were suspected. The bombing came amid a surge of militant attacks across Pakistan's northwest.

review.note: Dawn's October 30 report gives 117; later retrospective says 137. The existing 112 and demographic split require reconciliation, not certification.

title: Delhi serial bombings
description: Three bombs struck the Paharganj and Sarojini Nagar markets and a bus in the Govindpuri/Kalkaji area of Delhi on October 29, 2005, shortly before Diwali. Later reporting differs on the final death and injury totals.

review.note: PTI court coverage supports 67 deaths/over 225 injured, but other court reporting gives 62 and over 100; TOI gives 67/105. Original half-hour timing also conflicts with 17:30 to18:05 reporting. Core toll conflict is unresolved; remove unsupported tight timing.

title: Fort Hood Shooting
description: On November 5, 2009, Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan opened fire at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas, killing 13 people — 12 soldiers and one civilian — and wounding more than 30. Hasan, a US Army officer, was shot by responding police and survived. It was the deadliest mass shooting on a US military base; Hasan was convicted in 2013 of 13 counts of premeditated murder.

title: Baghlan bombing
description: A bombing targeted a parliamentary delegation visiting a sugar factory in Baghlan on November 6, 2007. Many children and several lawmakers died. UN reporting found that police and bodyguard gunfire after the explosion added to the casualties; the exact number killed by each cause was not established.

review.note: UNAMA's contemporaneous record and later Secretary-General report distinguish bombing deaths from subsequent police/bodyguard gunfire and use roughly70, not79. Exact split and final total remain uncertain; do not assign all deaths to bomber. UN investigation statements also differed before later reporting.

title: Pétion-Ville school collapse (Collège La Promesse Évangélique)
description: The College La Promesse Evangelique school in Petion-Ville collapsed during classes on November 7, 2008. An Inter Press Service report a year later put the death toll at 97, with more than 100 people injured. Earlier reports gave lower totals while rescue and recovery work continued.
sources: IFRC: Haiti school collapse information bulletin 1
AFP via La Nacion: November 10 toll update
Inter Press Service via Global Issues: one-year retrospective

title: Amman hotel bombings
description: Three suicide bombers attacked the lobbies of the Grand Hyatt, Radisson SAS and Days Inn hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing 60 people and injuring more than 100, including victims at a wedding reception in the Radisson. Al-Qaeda in Iraq claimed responsibility for the attacks.

title: Cyclone Sidr
description: Cyclone Sidr struck Bangladesh on November 15, 2007, causing destructive winds and coastal flooding. Officially reported death counts changed between assessments. Early fears that the toll might reach 15,000 were estimates, not confirmed fatalities.

review.note: 3,447 is a November20 provisional official count, later repeated by GFDRR; ADRC records3,363 onDecember29 and World Bank later3,406.15,000 was a feared early estimate, not a confirmed alternative tally. Date secure; final reported deaths/missing reconciliation remains needed.

title: Zasyadko mine explosion
description: A methane explosion at the Zasyadko coal mine in Donetsk on November 18, 2007, killed 101 miners, including one who died later in hospital. There were 457 miners underground when the explosion occurred. Later explosions in December are not included in this toll.

title: Xinxing Coal Mine Explosion
description: A gas explosion struck the Xinxing Coal Mine in Hegang, Heilongjiang, at about 2:30 a.m. local time on November 21, 2009 (November 20 UTC), while 528 miners were underground. The subsequent government investigation recorded 108 deaths and 133 injuries and identified serious safety and regulatory failures.

title: Sadr City bombings
description: Car bombs and mortar attacks struck Baghdad's Sadr City on the afternoon of November 23, 2006. Iraq Body Count records 215 deaths in the attacks.

title: Maguindanao Massacre
description: On November 23, 2009, armed men linked to the Ampatuan clan massacred 58 people in Maguindanao, Philippines, in an attack associated with the filing of Esmael Mangudadatu's gubernatorial candidacy. The victims included 32 journalists and media workers. CPJ describes it as the deadliest single attack on the press.

title: Mumbai attacks (26/11)
description: Ten Lashkar-e-Taiba attackers carried out coordinated attacks in Mumbai from November 26 to 29, 2008. The attacks killed 166 victims and injured 304 people. Nine attackers were killed during the operation, while Ajmal Kasab was captured alive.
sources: Bureau of Police Research and Development: Mumbai attack review
FBI: role and lessons learned in the Mumbai investigation

title: Dongfeng coal mine explosion
description: A coal-dust explosion at Dongfeng coal mine in Qitaihe, Heilongjiang, on November 27, 2005, killed 171 people and injured 48, according to the official investigation. The death toll included workers underground and at the surface.

title: Nevsky Express Bombing
description: On the night of November 27, 2009, a bomb equivalent to roughly 7 kg of TNT derailed the Nevsky Express train traveling from Moscow to St. Petersburg near Bologoye, killing 28 people and injuring about 90. Russian authorities declared the derailment a terrorist attack, blaming militants from the North Caucasus. It was the second bombing on the line, following an explosion in August 2007 that injured dozens.

review.note: Date, route, explosive cause and approximately 7 kg TNT corroborated. Reports give preliminary 25 then 26 and more than 100 wounded; final 28 and about 90 injuries not established by these sources. Do not substitute preliminary toll.

title: Super Typhoon Durian and Mayon mudflows
description: Typhoon Durian, known locally as Reming, struck the Philippines on November 30, 2006. Rain triggered destructive mudflows around Mayon Volcano. The Philippine disaster agency's report records 734 deaths and separately lists 762 people missing; the recorded death toll does not add the missing.

title: Lame Horse Nightclub Fire
description: A fire at the Lame Horse nightclub in Perm began early on December 5, 2009 local time, or December 4 UTC, after indoor pyrotechnics ignited ceiling material. Court reporting records 156 deaths.

title: Algiers bombings
description: Two car bombs struck Algiers on December 11, 2007, near the Constitutional Court and UN offices. The United Nations confirms that 17 of its staff were killed. Published overall death counts differ.

review.note: UN confirms17 staff andDecember11; anniversary message says20minutes between bombs, not10.37 is later official total, while secondary41 and early hospital67 differ. Exact overall toll cannot be established from UN staff-only memorial; remove unsupported exact interval.

title: Assassination of Benazir Bhutto
description: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto was assassinated as she left a campaign event in Rawalpindi on December 27, 2007. The UN commission of inquiry records 24 other people killed and 91 injured in the attack, giving 25 victims including Bhutto.
sources: UN Commission of Inquiry via Refworld

title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead) begins
description: Israel began Operation Cast Lead with airstrikes in Gaza on December 27, 2008 and launched a ground invasion on January 3, 2009. The offensive continued until January 18. B'Tselem's later accounting recorded 1,391 Palestinian deaths and 13 Israeli deaths across the conflict; official Israeli and earlier published Palestinian totals differed.

review.note: The December 27 start and January 3 ground invasion are supported by the IDF chronology; the toll covers the whole offensive through January 18, not only the opening day. The original 1,400 numerically combines an older B'Tselem count of 1,387 Palestinians with 13 Israelis. B'Tselem subsequently revised its Palestinian count to 1,391 (1,404 combined), while other B'Tselem pages contain older 1,385/1,390 figures; Israel's official total of 1,166 Palestinians also differs in inclusion and classification. Preserve those contradictions: this batch does not certify one exact total or reconcile civilian/child definitions. Remove outdated subtotals, the unverified 40-at-headquarters detail and the compressed UN legal conclusion. Toll and geographic scope remain unresolved for integration.

sources.name: B'Tselem: September 2009 casualty release, with update notice
B'Tselem: Gaza Strip background and updated conflict totals
Israel Defense Forces: Operation Cast Lead chronology
